patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Fastmail and Vonage share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose Fastmail only if your buying job matches “Privacy-focused business email, calendar and contacts with custom domains and shared addre” rather than Vonage's shape. Choose Vonage only if your buying job matches “SMB/mid VoIP business phone (VBC) — Mobile from $13.99/line/mo on 12-month promo; Premium/” rather than Fastmail's shape. Workflow advantage: Fastmail leans shared coverage; Vonage leans business-phone, sales-calling. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Fastmail and Vonage share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Fastmail is Privacy-focused business email, calendar and contacts with custom domains and shared addresses — Business Basic from $3/user/month annual; a; Vonage is SMB/mid VoIP business phone (VBC) — Mobile from $13.99/line/mo on 12-month promo; Premium/Advanced higher..
- Company-size focus: Fastmail (micro, small-business) vs Vonage (solo, small-business, mid-market).
- Workflow coverage skew: Fastmail-leaning — vs Vonage-leaning business-phone, sales-calling.
- Researched limits: Fastmail — Not a business phone, WhatsApp or team-chat product — adjacent to business communications; Vonage — Taxes and regulatory fees sit on top of published per-line floors.

Limitations — Fastmail: Not a business phone, WhatsApp or team-chat product — adjacent to business communications; Shared addresses, shared calendars and the shared address book require Standard or above; Vonage: Taxes and regulatory fees sit on top of published per-line floors; Call recording and deeper CRM land on Advanced / Premium packaging.

Poor-fit cases: Fastmail is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Not a business phone, WhatsApp or team-chat product — adjacent to business communications · Vonage is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Taxes and regulatory fees sit on top of published per-line floors · Avoid Fastmail if you actually need Vonage's motion (SMB/mid VoIP business phone (VBC) — Mobile from $13.99/line/mo on 12-month promo)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
